messages:
irene: FYI alert just fired for hosted-infer us-west-2 - p99 timeout SLO burn + 5xx uptick from 00:12-00:20 UTC. customers reporting timeouts and 502/504s. Filing here so we have a single thread.
julia-observability: looking at the grafana now — total 5xx fraction jumped from ~0.2% -> 3.6% at 00:12. latency p95 stayed fine but p99 exploded. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/hosted-infer/slo-overview
samir: any recent deploys? deploy bot?
deploy-bot: deploy completed: commit 7f4d2a3 (ingress-prefetch): finished 00:05 UTC, rollout to us-west-2 completed 00:07 UTC
louise-support: multiple customers opened tickets during window, examples include customer A, customer B. They see immediate 504 on single-shot generation requests, but retries sometimes succeed.
julia-observability: log query I ran (cloud-logs):
```
resource.type="k8s_container" labels.cluster="usw2" | filter http_status >= 500 | parse path as path | stats count() by path, upstream_cluster
```
results show most 5xx are from upstream_cluster="model-proxy-v2" and path starts with "/v1/generate"
samir: tracing gaps: a bunch of requests have no spans from kv-cache service. looks like parent span missing which aligns with prefetch/handshake race. trace sampling still records head request that times out but child spans for model-proxy are absent.
julia-observability: related metric: model-proxy handshake latencies spiked at same time (handshake.millis p99 from 40ms -> 800ms). suggests connection churn or pool exhaustion.
matt-platform: last change to connection pooling was in 7f4d2a3 — we increased pool size but also added aggressive idle eviction. could be eviction too aggressive under load and causing re-handshakes.
loise-support: reproducer from a customer:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":5}'
```
returns 504 intermittently during spike. they included trace-id header x-trace-id: 01ab...
samir: steps to triage: 1) pin traffic to older model-proxy variant (fallback), 2) bump model-proxy connection pool and disable idle-evict for 15m, 3) enable extra tracing for handshake path to capture parent spans. can we do 1 & 2 as quick mitigation?
matt-platform: I can push a rollback of the idle-evict flag to us-west-2 canary within 5m.
julia-observability: will add temporary log filter to capture missing-span trace-ids and export to support with a quick query. query to grab example traces:
```
proto.trace_span where name="handshake" and duration>200ms | limit 100
```
irene: please post any chosen trace-ids here so support can correlate to customer tickets. also note SLO page for the customer is in edgenet-org-123.
louise-support: posting two trace ids we got from customer A: 01ab2c3d4e and 01ab2c3d4f. they map to requests at 00:14:23 and 00:16:09 UTC.
samir: got them. pulling raw logs for those traces now.
matt-platform: rollback flag pushed to canary-1, monitoring. will promote if no new regressions in 2m.
julia-observability: created a temporary alert to catch handshake span drops: if missing_span_ratio > 0.5% over 5m for us-west-2 -> page.
irene: good. keep this thread updated. after mitigation we should run load replay against canary to validate.
samir: initial logs show model-proxy returned 502 with upstream timeout for those trace ids. also saw TLS handshake errors in a few entries - possibly transient cert chain validation; collecting more.
louise-support: customers updated: one docs engineer confirms retries are working but unhappy. asked for ETA for fix.
matt-platform: will hold the canary and escalate to infra if we see cert TTL or rotation issues. next actions: 1) continue tracing capture, 2) share repro curl with token and trace header to infra, 3) escalate certs if TLS errors persist.
irene: thanks team — I'll keep ops and support looped and update the incident board. :thumbsup:
